Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Counter affidavits filed by learned counsel for the respondents in Criminal Appeal No.11179 of 2023 & Criminal Appeal No.11795 of 2023 today are taken on record.
These criminal appeals are being heard together and are being decided by this common order.

Heard Sri R.B. Singh, Sri Ramesh Chandra Pal & Sri Mohd. Bilal, learned counsel for the appellants as well as Sri Gorakh Yadav, learned counsel for all the respondents alongwith learned A.G.A. and perused the entire record.
These criminal appeals under Section 14-A (2) Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act have been preferred by the appellants with the prayer to set aside the bail rejection order dated 09.10.2023 & 11.08.2023 passed by the learned Additional Session Judge/Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Ghaziabad.

sentences.text: It is submitted that in this case the land in dispute was purchased by father of the informant in the year 1992 from the mother of Neelu & Naresh.

Further submitted that mutation order was also passed but on account of reluctance on the part of the revenue authority it could not be entered in the revenue record as a result the land remained in the name of appellants.
Thereafter, in the year 2023 they executed sale deeds in favour of Moolchand even with the knowledge that land was already purchased by the father of the informant.
In this way, the appellants committed fraud with the informant and threatening him to dispossess from the land whereas he is in possession of the land in question.
Further submitted that the dispute relating to land between the parties is purely of civil nature, therefore, no offence u/s 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C. is made out against them.
Even the sale deeds are not cancelled by any competent court and no any such proceedings have been initiated by the informant side at all.
Learned civil court is to decide as to who is real owner of the land in question and has the authority to execute the sale deed.
Entire allegations levelled in the F.I.R. and in the statement are false.

The Court below while passing the impugned order did not take Amit Kumar vs State Of U.P. And Another on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166878586/
2 into account the facts and evidence available on record in right perspective and erred in passing the same.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellants also referred to the amended provisions of SC/ST Act.
Appellants are in jail since 06.10.2023 & 28.07.2023.
It is lastly submitted that the impugned order rejecting the bail applications of the appellants suffers from infirmity and illegality warranting interference by this Court.

Learned counsel for the respondents as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid and contended that in this case the land in question was already sold in favour of father of the informant and order regarding mutation was also passed but the revenue authority failed to make entry of the order in revenue record that was the reason it remained in the name of appellants and they fraudulently executed sale deeds in favour of other persons knowing that they had no authority in this regard.
In this way, they are not innocent and it can also not be said that they transferred the land in good faith.

All these facts were considered by the learned Special Judge SC/ST Act while rejecting the bail of the appellants, therefore, there is no any illegality and impropriety in the order but these criminal appeals being devoid of merit are liable to be dismissed.
I have considered the rival submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the entire record including the impugned order carefully.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused, severity of punishment, the orders passed by learned Special Judge, the nature of dispute between the parties, this Court is of the opinion that the appellants have made out a case for bail.
The Court below erred in rejecting the bail application.
The impugned orders dated 09.10.2023 & 11.08.2023 suffer from infirmity and illegality and the same are liable to be set-aside and the appeals are to be allowed.
Accordingly, all the four appeals are allowed and the impugned orders rejecting the bail applications of the appellants are, hereby, set-aside.

Let the appellants- Amit Kumar, Leelu, Smt. Rajo & Naresh involved in Case Crime No.135 of 2023,
under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120B, 504, 506 I.P.C. and 3(2)(5) SC/ST Act, Police Station Bhojpur, District Ghaziabad, be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two heavy sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
1. The appellants will not tamper with the evidence during the trial.
2. The appellants will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution witness.
3. The appellants will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
4. The appellants shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused, or suspected, of the commission of which he is suspected.
